title: Interview Preparation Kit Check
description: Predict how the IPK organizes practice and which track a topic keyword should route to.

questions.prompt: How does the Interview Preparation Kit organize its problems?

options.text: By difficulty level only
By topic, so you can practice one recurring pattern at a time
Randomly, to simulate a real OA
By company that requested the problems

questions.explanation: IPK groups problems by topic (Arrays, Strings, DP, ...) so each session reinforces one pattern.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the `Warmup` set inside IPK?

options.text: The hardest problems, reserved for experts
The easiest entry problems, meant to build momentum
A timed proctored certification
A random mix of every topic

questions.explanation: Warmup problems are intentionally easy — they exist to build momentum, not to test depth.

questions.prompt: If you're weak specifically on array manipulation, what's the most efficient next step?

options.text: Work through the kit strictly top-to-bottom regardless of topic
Route directly into the Arrays track
Repeat the Warmup set until it feels easy
Skip IPK entirely and take a certification instead

questions.explanation: IPK's topic-first structure lets you target a known weak spot directly instead of grinding unrelated problems.

questions.prompt: A topic keyword doesn't match `arrays`, `strings`, or `warmup`. What should a topic router do?

options.text: Throw an error — only three topics are valid
Route it into a general/mixed catch-all bucket
Default to the Warmup track
Ignore the input silently

questions.explanation: Unrecognized topics fall into a general/mixed bucket by design rather than failing outright.

questions.prompt: Why does IPK organize practice by topic instead of by difficulty like score bands do?

options.text: Topic and difficulty are the same thing on HackerRank
Focused, pattern-based practice targets specific interview weaknesses better than a difficulty sort
Difficulty sorting is not possible in IPK
IPK doesn't allow you to see problem difficulty

questions.explanation: Interview prep benefits from reinforcing one recurring pattern at a time, which topic grouping enables and difficulty grouping doesn't.
